1

ONLINE PRESENTATION
The presentation (PPT) offered a thorough and detailed overview of Citi and how it
operates. They discussed different aspects, including what Citi does, the structure of
their operations, and the testing platform they use. It's highly recommended to attend the
PPT because if you're chosen, you might face HR questions that require knowledge
about the company. The key takeaways from the presentation are understanding the
company's work, your role there, the company's culture, mission, and values. This
information will certainly benefit you in your HR interview.
ONLINE ASSESSMENT
Criteria:
●
No active backlogs and CPI > 6
●
No Branch Restriction
Assessment Pattern:
The test comprised 05 sections, each with its own timer, and no switching between sections was
permitted. Navigation between sections was not allowed, and there was no penalty for incorrect
answers. The test was administered on the AMCAT platform and included camera monitoring.
●
Core CS MCQs (25 Questions in 35 Minutes) :
○
Questions based on CS fundamentals like DBMS, OOPS, Operating
Systems, Debugging, Output Prediction, Data Structures, etc.
○
You should be really crisp and clear with your basics to pass this section.
○
Questions were of moderate complexity.
●
Aptitude (16 Questions in 16 Minutes):
○
Questions based on basic mathematics like profit-loss, permutations and
combinations, percentages, data interpretations, etc.
○
You can tackle all these questions if you are fast with your mathematical
calculations.
●
Logical Reasoning (14 Questions in 14 Minutes):
2

○
Questions
were
based
on
analyzing
and
identifying
patterns,
relationships,series and sequences.
○
Questions were of easy to moderate difficulty.
○
Try to solve all these questions as there is no negative marking and you
can do all these questions, if calculated risk is taken.
●
Verbal Reasoning (22 Questions in 18 Minutes):
○
These were to evaluate language and comprehension skills. Questions
involved synonyms/antonyms, completing sentences, prepositions, etc.
○
There were two passages, each with 3-4 questions which are easily doable
once the passage is carefully read.
●
Coding Section (2 Questions in 60 Minutes): First question is of easy level and
second question is of medium to high difficulty.
○
Trapezium Pattern Printing (link): This question has been repeated by Citi for
the past 2-3 years. Try to solve the first question in less than 15 minutes. I was
able to clear all test cases.
○
Maximum Toll Revenue : There are N cities with unique city codes from 1 to
N and are connected by N-1 roads. The road network is in the form of a tree
which connects two cities. A path is a road, combination of roads,
connecting two cities.Each road has a toll booth that collects a toll equal to
the maximum number of paths of which that particular road is a part. We
need to identify the road which 3 collects maximum toll revenue(output is a
pair of cities connected by road). If two or more toll booths collect the same
total revenue, then we have to print the pair of cities with lexicographically
smaller city codes. The inputs to the tree were taken like a graph
(adjacency list) unlike a node based tree.The way of taking input did
confuse a lot of people,this had also happened in a previous test.
I was able to clear 08/13 test cases for this question.
76 students were shortlisted for the interviews.
3

TECHNICAL INTERVIEW
Before sitting for an interview, ensure that you are well-acquainted with the content on
your resume. Additionally, try to do a little LinkedIn search to familiarize yourself with
your interviewer's profile. The interviewer had an extensive background in React
spanning over 8 years, which was closely aligned with my domain expertise.
The interview started with a direct focus on my resume, where my React-related work
and projects garnered notable enthusiasm from the interviewer.
After the introduction, the interviewer proceeded with summing five questions and
asking at once. I vividly recall these questions:
➔Provide an overview of yourself.
➔Elaborate on your strengths and how they have positively influenced your journey.
➔Discuss your areas of improvement or weaknesses.
➔Describe your skill set.
➔Delve into the details of one of your team projects and challenges you faced..
In a composed manner, I systematically addressed each of these five questions,
demonstrating my ability to recall and response in sequence. I was able to answer all
these five questions in two minutes.
Subsequently, the conversation shifted towards a deep dive into the MERN stack,
particularly focusing on React. This segment extended for about six minutes and the
interviewer fully evaluated my familiarity and proficiency in the subject matter.
The discussion transitioned to programming languages, and I highlighted my usage of
C++. The interviewer then presented a straightforward programming question: Write code
to find exponent x^y (pow(x,y)) .
I began by outlining a basic approach utilizing loops and progressed to explaining a
more optimized solution using binary operators. I shared my screen and efficiently coded
the optimized solution on the Sublime text editor. This took around 3-4 minutes.
The overall interview duration was around 15 minutes, during which I felt that I was able
to make a positive impression on the interviewer. As the interview drew to a close, the
4

interviewer encouraged me to ask questions.I took the opportunity to inquire about the
expected tech stack for interns upon joining, showcasing my keen interest in the
company's technological landscape.
31 students were selected for the next round with simultaneous calling for next
rounds.
Amid simultaneous tech interviews, candidates progressed to round two swiftly. Despite a
planned 25-30 minute gap, my second-round call arrived within 5 minutes. Swiftly preparing,
I joined the meeting. So make sure that you stay readily dressed and prepared during the
process.
HR INTERVIEW
At the start I encountered some headphone issues which the interviewer patiently
awaited while I resolved them.The interviewer displayed a friendly and amiable
demeanor, she gave me some time to cool down.
The interview began with the interviewer's introduction and then she Inquired about my
introduction and prior round's experience. The conversation transitioned to discussing
my strengths and weaknesses.
Subsequently, she probed into my hobbies, catching me off guard. I mentioned my
enjoyment of philosophical book reading, though uncertain if it qualified as a hobby for
this interview. Interestingly, our discussion delved into this topic, as she shared my
interest. The dialogue expanded to cover subjects such as capitalism, neo-Marxism,
feminism, among others. During all these discussions, somehow all my answers revolved
around the core values of Citi which made the interviewer impressed.
The session concluded with inquiries about higher studies plans and rationale for
choosing Citi. Content with my responses, she invited my queries, which, unprepared, I
refrained from posing.
Finally I was one of 15 students selected for the internship.
5

Preparation Resources
DSA: It is important for your online assessment tests as well as your interview rounds..Try
to not get confused with plenty of resources available on the internet. I followed these
resources:
●
Leetcode Blind 75
●
Striver SDE Sheet or DSA Sheet by Arash Goyal
CS Fundamentals: Some companies ask questions from these topics in their
assessment rounds in MCQ Format. Mainly questions are asked in interview rounds from
this topic. It includes Computer Science core subjects like Operating Systems, OOPS,
Data Structures and Algorithms (theory), DBMS, CN(not important for internships) - basics
only .
●
Follow Interviewbit sheets which are easily available on simple google search or
this github repo also have all resources.
●
If you want video content you can follow either gate smashers or love babbar, they
have playlists on each subject.
APTITUDE: For this try to solve questions in your free time. Try here
TIPS:
●
In your assessments, for MCQ rounds try to be as fast as possible when there is
no negative marking and in case of negative marking try to take calculated risk by
eliminating the incorrect options.
●
For coding questions, try to start by taking a look at all the questions and then with
a basic approach if you don’t have any idea of how to solve a question.
●
In technical interviews, take your time to explain questions asked. Never get
puzzled in your words. Think before speaking while explaining.
●
Be prepared with your projects and questions like: your motivation behind
creating those, tech stack used by you, why that tech stack, etc.
●
Read company archives as companies repeat questions and have a specific
pattern of hiring.
6

●
Give mock interviews to your seniors (they are there for you) , friends.
●
Try to take advice from seniors, they are always ready to help whenever you need.
INTERNSHIP EXPERIENCE:
My internship at Citi was an amazing experience. I learned a lot about corporate dynamics and
had the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technologies. I also got to collaborate with a
diverse team of people and learn from their different perspectives.
One of the highlights of my internship was the opportunity to work on end-user web applications.
This gave me a chance to apply my skills in Angular, Typescript, shell scripting, and PL/SQL. I also
learned a lot about Oracle SQL databases.
My manager, mentor, and buddy were all very supportive and helpful. They made sure that I was
able to get up to speed quickly and that I had everything I needed to succeed.
I was also really impressed by the culture at Citi. It was very collaborative and supportive.
Everyone was always willing to help each other out.
After completion of my internship, PPOs were offered after a week. I was also one of 13 students
who were offered a Pre-Placement Offer (PPO). This was a huge honor and it made me feel really
good about my work.
Overall, my internship at Citi was an amazing experience. I learned a lot, made great connections,
and had a lot of fun. I'm so grateful for the opportunity and I would definitely recommend it to
anyone who is looking for a challenging and rewarding internship.
